q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "She did not knew the answer to the last question."
o: She did not known the answer to the last question.
She does not knew the answer to the last question.
She did not know the answer to the last question.
She did not knowing the answer to the last question.
x: After the helping verb 'did', the main verb takes its base form: 'did not know'. The past tense is already shown by 'did'.

q: Identify the error in this sentence: "Ayesha is senior than me by two years in college."
o: 'by two years' should be 'from two years'
'in college' should be 'at the college of'
x: Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior are followed by 'to', not 'than'. The rest of the sentence is correct.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "I am looking forward to meet you at the conference."
o: I am looking forward to meeting you at the conference.
I am looking forward for meeting you at the conference.
I am looking forward to met you at the conference.
I am looking forward meet you at the conference.
x: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by an -ing form: 'looking forward to meeting'.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "The new hostel has many furnitures in every room."
o: The new hostel has a lot of furniture in every room.
The new hostel has many furniture in every room.
The new hostel has a lot of furnitures in every room.
The new hostel has much furnitures in every room.
x: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun: it has no plural form and takes 'much' or 'a lot of', not 'many'.

q: Identify the error in this sentence: "Bilal has been absent from college since three days."
o: 'since three days' should be 'for three days'
x: 'For' is used with a length of time (three days); 'since' is used with a point in time (Monday, 2020). 'Absent from' is the correct preposition.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "Unless you do not revise regularly, you will forget the formulas."
o: Unless you will revise regularly, you will forget the formulas.
Unless you not revise regularly, you will forget the formulas.
Unless you revise regularly, you will forget the formulas.
Unless you do not revise regularly, you forget the formulas.
x: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so adding 'do not' makes a double negative that reverses the meaning. The verb after 'unless' stays in the present simple.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "No sooner did the guests arrive when the lights went out."
o: No sooner had the guests arrived when the lights went out.
No sooner the guests had arrived than the lights went out.
No sooner did the guests arrived than the lights went out.
No sooner had the guests arrived than the lights went out.
x: 'No sooner' is paired with 'than', not 'when', and for one past action before another it takes inverted past perfect: 'No sooner had the guests arrived than...'.

q: Which question tag correctly completes the sentence? "Let's go for a walk after dinner, ____?"
x: A suggestion beginning with 'Let's' (let us) takes the tag 'shall we?'. 'Isn't it' is a common error and does not match any verb in the sentence.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "The reason he failed the test is because he did not revise."
o: The reason he failed the test is due to he did not revise.
The reason why he failed the test is because of he did not revise.
The reason he failed the test is that he did not revise.
The reason he failed the test because he did not revise.
x: 'The reason ... is because' repeats the idea of cause; correct usage is 'The reason ... is that ...'. The last version has no main verb for 'the reason', so it is not a complete sentence.

q: Which group of words cannot stand on its own as a sentence?
o: Because the lift was not working.
The lift was not working, so we used the stairs.
We used the stairs because the lift was not working.
x: A clause beginning with 'because' depends on a main clause and cannot stand alone. The other three each contain a complete main clause.

q: Which option correctly corrects the comma splice in "The shop was closed, we went home."?
o: The shop was closed, we so went home.
The shop was closed, and so went home.
The shop was closed, so we went home.
The shop being closed, so we went home.
x: Two main clauses cannot be joined by a comma alone; adding the conjunction 'so' after the comma fixes it. 'And so went home' has lost its subject, and 'being closed, so' mixes two structures.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "The job needs patience, skill and being honest."
o: The job needs patience, skill and to be honest.
The job needs patience, skill and honesty.
The job needs being patient, skill and honesty.
The job needs patience, skilful and honesty.
x: Items in a list should have the same grammatical form (parallel structure). 'Patience', 'skill' and 'honesty' are all nouns.

q: Which sentence says clearly that Sara, and nobody else, passed the test?
x: 'Only' should stand next to the word it limits; placed before 'Sara', it means no one else passed. In the other positions it limits the verb or 'the test' instead.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "To get a good score, regular practice must be done."
o: To get a good score, regular practice must be done by it.
To get a good score, regular practice is must.
To getting a good score, you must practise regularly.
To get a good score, you must practise regularly.
x: The opening phrase 'To get a good score' needs a person as the subject who does the getting; 'regular practice' cannot get a score. Adding 'you' as subject removes the dangling modifier.

q: Which sentence correctly combines "The doctor was very kind." and "She treated my mother."?
o: The doctor who treated my mother was very kind.
The doctor which treated my mother was very kind.
The doctor whom treated my mother was very kind.
The doctor, she treated my mother, was very kind.
x: 'Who' is the relative pronoun for a person acting as subject. 'Which' is for things, 'whom' is an object form, and the last version adds an extra pronoun 'she'.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "She is good both at chemistry as well as physics."
o: She is good both at chemistry and as well as physics.
She is good at both chemistry as well as physics.
She is both good at chemistry as well as at physics.
She is good at both chemistry and physics.
x: 'Both' is paired with 'and', never with 'as well as', and it should come just before the two things joined: 'at both chemistry and physics'.

q: Choose the correct version of this sentence: "By studying every night is how she passed the exam."
o: By studying every night was how she passed the exam.
By studying every night, is how she passed the exam.
Studying every night is how by she passed the exam.
She passed the exam by studying every night.
x: A phrase beginning with 'By' cannot be the subject of 'is'; this mixes two structures. 'She passed the exam by studying every night' has a clear subject and verb.

q: Which sentence makes it clear that Ali, not Bilal, was ill?
o: Ali told Bilal that he was ill.
Bilal was told by Ali that he was ill.
Ali and Bilal said that he was ill.
x: In direct speech 'I' can only mean the speaker, Ali. In the other sentences 'he' could refer to either boy, so the meaning is unclear.

q: Complete the sentence: "My elder brother ____ in a bank in Karachi."
x: 'My elder brother' is a singular third-person subject, so the present-simple verb takes -s: 'works'.

q: Complete the sentence: "A box of pencils ____ been placed on each desk."
x: The subject is 'a box', which is singular; 'of pencils' only describes it. So the verb is 'has been placed'.

q: Complete the sentence: "Mathematics ____ my favourite subject this year."
x: Names of subjects ending in -s, such as mathematics, physics and economics, are singular and take a singular verb.

q: Complete the sentence: "The doctor and the nurse ____ waiting outside the ward."
x: Repeating 'the' shows two different people joined by 'and', so the subject is plural and takes 'are'.

q: Complete the sentence: "The number of applicants for the course ____ risen sharply this year."
x: 'The number of ...' refers to one number, so it is singular: 'has risen'. It is 'a number of' (meaning many) that takes a plural verb.

q: Complete the sentence: "Somebody ____ left the tap running in the laboratory."
x: Indefinite pronouns such as somebody, someone and everybody are singular, so the verb is 'has left'.

q: Complete the sentence: "Neither Ali nor I ____ ready for the test."
x: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is 'I', so the verb is 'am'.

q: Complete the sentence: "The girl who sings in the choir and plays the sitar ____ my cousin."
x: The main subject is 'the girl'; 'who sings ... and plays the sitar' describes her. A singular subject takes 'is'.

q: In which sentence does the verb agree with its subject?
o: The scissors is on the table.
The scissors are on the table.
Your glasses is on the desk.
x: Nouns for things made of two matching parts, such as scissors, glasses and trousers, are plural and take plural verbs: 'the scissors are'.

q: Choose the correct spelling to fill the blank: "Did you ____ my letter last week?"
x: The correct spelling is 'receive': the rule is 'i before e except after c', so after 'c' it is 'ei'.

q: Choose the correct word: "Pens, paper and envelopes are sold at the ____ shop."
x: 'Stationery' (with -ery) means writing materials. 'Stationary' (with -ary) is an adjective meaning not moving.

q: Choose the correct word: "After the operation, the patient is recovering ____."
x: An adverb is needed to describe how the patient is recovering. 'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective and 'goodness' is a noun.

q: Choose the correct word form: "His ____ to arrive on time cost him the job."
x: After the possessive 'His', a noun is needed as the subject of 'cost'. 'Failure' is the noun; the other options are verb forms.

q: Choose the correct spelling to fill the blank: "Keep raw meat ____ from cooked food."
x: The correct spelling is 'separate', with 'a' after the 'p' and again before the 't'. 'Seperate' is a very common misspelling.

q: Choose the correct spelling to fill the blank: "It is a great ____ to study at this medical college."
x: The correct spelling is 'privilege': p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e, with no 'd' and with 'i' then 'e' in the middle syllables.

q: Choose the correct word: "The lecture was so ____ that half the class fell asleep."
x: An -ing adjective describes what causes the feeling: the lecture was 'boring'. The students would be 'bored', which describes how a person feels.

q: Choose the correct word: "The new medicine had no ____ on his fever."
x: After 'no', a noun is needed: 'effect' means a result. 'Affect' is normally a verb, and 'effective' and 'effectively' are adjective and adverb forms.
